clue.text: Open up book and carp?

parts.note: the roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A request to open a book and complain about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like a verb meaning grumble, but it is the fish; the roach belongs to the carp family, which the question mark concedes.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject or a cask is to open it up, a standard synonym.

clue.text: I'm sincere but mistaken in talk about past

indicators.note: the phrase I'm sincere is declared mistaken, so its letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests their sincerity while being wrong about history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but mistaken' tells you to rearrange the nine letters of I'M SINCERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to talk fondly about past events, an exact verb synonym.

clue.text: Further article warning against woman?

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
'not' is the word used to warn against doing something, as in 'not that!'
her stands for a woman, a pronoun

explanation.surface: Another piece of writing cautioning against a particular woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means one more or further, as in another helping.

clue.text: Very popular TV presenter disowning son

indicators.note: the presenter disowns, that is drops, the letter for son

parts.note: a host presents a television show
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A celebrity broadcaster publicly rejects their own child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disowning son' removes S from HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is informal for very much in demand or fashionable, a close synonym.

clue.text: Expression of protest at footballer's return appearance

parts.note: 'come, come!' is an exclamation of mild protest
a back is a defensive football player

explanation.surface: Fans protest at a footballer returning to the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expression of protest' gives COME, as in 'come now!'; 'footballer's' gives BACK, a defender.
explanation.definitionFit: A comeback is a return, especially of a performer or sportsperson, after time away.

clue.text: Exclamation over endless pleasure to be had in holiday venue

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: pleasure loses its last letter

parts.note: fun means pleasure

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about the boundless enjoyment on offer at a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts N from FUN to give FU; 'over' puts COR above it in this down answer. COR is British slang, an exclamation like 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island popular as a holiday destination, an example of the category.

clue.text: Meets a price, after wrangling, for major artwork

indicators.note: the words meets a price are wrangled, argued over and twisted, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A buyer pays the asking price after haggling over a great painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after wrangling' signals an anagram of MEETS A PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece is an artist's finest or a supremely skilled work, a direct synonym.

clue.text: US city increasingly noticeable in reports

indicators.note: reports are spoken accounts, so the word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: bolder means more striking, standing out more

explanation.surface: An American city is said to be ever more prominent.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLDER said aloud gives the city's name; 'in reports' signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Boulder is a city in Colorado, an example of a US city.

clue.text: Pink and black material will be about right

indicators.note: coal goes about, around, the letter for right

parts.note: coal is black fuel

explanation.surface: A fabric description: pink and black together will look right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' looks like a colour of fabric paired with black, but it is the definition; 'about' wraps COAL round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral names a pinkish-orange colour, taken from the marine material.

clue.text: I'm taking letters to the soldiers — one's a fake

parts.note: taken as written
post means mail, letters
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone carries the mail to the troops while confessing to being a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword shorthand for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: An impostor is a person who pretends to be someone else, so is a fake.

clue.text: Jet's second to leave with monarch on board

indicators.note: the monarch is taken on board, inside, the word for leave

parts.note: to quit is to leave
R is short for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A jet aircraft's co-pilot steps off when the king boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' suggests an aeroplane, but it is a spurt of liquid. 'on board' puts R inside QUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirt is a thin jet of liquid forced out, a synonym of jet.

clue.text: Where slates are free?

parts.note: roof slates sit literally atop a building, and the same phrase is the idiom for something given without charge

explanation.surface: A riddle about roofing tiles costing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Slates are roof tiles, which sit on top of a building; the phrase for that position is also the idiom meaning paid for by the establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means free of charge, paid for by the bar or restaurant, and slates literally lie atop a dwelling.

clue.text: Channel broadcasting good news is a sensible course

parts.note: news that is good makes one happy
a medium is a spiritualist who acts as a channel to the dead, or any channel of communication

explanation.surface: A TV station that only broadcasts cheerful stories is wisely run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like a TV station, but a medium is a channel of communication; one broadcasting good news is a cheerful one.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy medium is a compromise between extremes, the sensible middle course.

clue.text: Artist recalled by one youngster

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the letters are taken in the opposite order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a lad is a young boy

explanation.surface: A painter is remembered by a single young person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns I LAD round to give the surrealist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dali was a Spanish surrealist painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: One getting benefit from University series

explanation.surface: A student benefits from a university's programme of lectures.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who makes use of, and so gains from, something.

clue.text: Rich island ruler taking on America

parts.note: Prospero rules the island in Shakespeare's The Tempest
US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A wealthy island leader makes a deal with the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: PROSPERO is the exiled duke who rules an island in Shakespeare's The Tempest; 'taking on' adds US.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means wealthy and successful, a synonym of rich.

clue.text: Eggs polished off, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase says the word is heard rather than read, so it is spelt differently

parts.note: something polished off is finished, over

explanation.surface: Someone has wolfed down a plate of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent OVER and the plural of ovum sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the plural of ovum, an egg cell, so it means eggs.

clue.text: Thumb twiddling with yarn, yarn given an unlikely twist

indicators.note: twiddling means twisting idly, so the letters of thumb and yarn are turned about

explanation.surface: Someone twiddles their thumbs while spinning a tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twiddling' rearranges THUMB and the first YARN; 'with' joins them. The second 'yarn' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban myth is a widely circulated but untrue story, a tale with an improbable twist.

clue.text: The way one walks when feeling nostalgic?

definitions.text: The way one walks when feeling nostalgic?

parts.words: The way one walks when feeling nostalgic?
parts.note: the clue pretends to ask about a route on foot, but means the imagined path of recollection taken when longing for the past

explanation.surface: A question about where a sentimental person likes to stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip down this road is the idiom for nostalgically recalling past times.

clue.text: In part, fail to convince old woman to attend court

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An actor in a role fails to persuade an elderly lady to appear in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' means while playing a role; 'to attend' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to play a role too theatrically, so the performance fails to convince.

clue.text: Taverns, British, involved in endless promotion

indicators.note: the letter for British is involved in, placed inside, the shortened word
promotion loses its last letter

parts.note: a push is a promotional drive or campaign

explanation.surface: British bars caught up in non-stop advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts H from PUSH to give PUS; 'involved in' places B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs are public houses, the everyday word for taverns.

clue.text: Artist's picture: a ship, nothing more

parts.note: pic is short for picture
taken as written
SS stands for steamship
O is the round figure zero, nothing at all

explanation.surface: A painter's work shows a single ship and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Artist's' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Competent story, though one's not following at first

indicators.note: the letter for following is not there, so it is removed from the story
the removed letter is the opening one of the story

parts.note: a fable is a story
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A capable tale, though one character fails to keep up at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not following at first' drops F, the opening letter, from FABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means having the skill to do something, a synonym of competent.

clue.text: Left after excellent Scottish fight

indicators.note: the letter for left comes after the Scots word

parts.note: braw is Scots for fine or excellent

explanation.surface: A great Scottish scrap breaks out after someone leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAW is a Scots word meaning fine or splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rough noisy fight, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Our mother caught a new fragrance evaporating slowly

indicators.note: Eve has caught, taken in, the next letters

parts.note: Eve is the biblical mother of humankind
taken as written
scent means fragrance

explanation.surface: Mum caught a whiff of a new perfume that faded gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our mother' is Eve of Genesis, mother of all; 'caught' signals that she holds the next letters inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Evanescent means fading quickly away from sight or memory, as a vapour vanishes.

clue.text: Warning to traffic: tilt of road with top layer missing

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a camber is the slope of a road surface

explanation.surface: A road sign warns that the tilted surface has lost its asphalt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with top layer missing' removes C, the top letter of CAMBER in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is the traffic-light colour warning drivers to prepare to stop.

clue.text: Meat product I'm unfortunately returning

indicators.note: returning signals the letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
alas expresses regret, unfortunately

explanation.surface: Someone sadly brings back a cured sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the whole run backwards, not each word separately; 'Meat product' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, seasoned sausage, an example of a processed meat.

clue.text: See what the nice she-elephant catches — a sweet?

definitions.text: See what the nice she-elephant catches
definitions.meaning: a female elephant who is nice attracts the attention of a male elephant, catching its gaze
a hard peppermint boiled sweet with stripes, popular in Britain

explanation.surface: A fond look at a female elephant who wins a male admirer and a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: A male elephant is a bull, so the attractive cow catches his eye. The second meaning is a traditional British hard striped mint sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pachyderm male's gaze and the name of a striped British boiled mint share this spelling.

clue.text: He left his wife without a backward glance that's fate!

definitions.text: He left his wife without a backward glance
definitions.meaning: in Genesis this man fled Sodom without looking back, while his wife turned to look and became a pillar of salt
one's portion or destiny in life

explanation.surface: A man walks out on his spouse without regret; such is destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible story: the man escaping Sodom never looked back, but his wife did and was turned to salt, so he left her behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical nephew of Abraham, and the everyday word for one's destiny or portion.

clue.text: Hourglass? One's no longer in service

definitions.meaning: an hourglass is an ancient device for measuring time, read whimsically
a veteran who has retired from active work

explanation.surface: An antique sand clock described as retired.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical reading of an hourglass as an ancient timekeeping device.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a veteran, and literally an ancient timekeeping device.

clue.text: Work hard in attempt to secure cup

indicators.note: the attempt holds, secures, the other letters inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
op is short for opus, a work
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A team toils hard in an effort to win the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is short for opus, a musical work; 'to secure' signals the attempt holding the other letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a prize such as a cup awarded for winning a contest.
